title: Jack as Fortune-teller
year_evidence: 扉に『PUBLISHED BY THE AMERICAN FOLK-LORE SOCIETY … 1924』、序文の署名に『April, 1924.』
text:
T. Brown, Claremont, St. Anne.

Der was a day Jack says he was a fortune-teller. De king call him dat
his wife los’ her marriage ring and he want him to tell him where it
go. Jack didn’t know not’ing all de same, but jus’ working his head. De
king got t’ree servant in his house. De t’ree of dem steal de ring. De
king give Jack four days to tell him. One mo’ning, one carry Jack
breakfas’. Jack says, “Praise de Lord, I got one!” Same day, one carry
his dinner; same day, one carry his supper. Jack says, “Praise de Lord,
I got de t’ree!” (Jack meant he get t’ree meals, but de servant think
Jack mean them.) One of the servant go in the house, say, “Let us tell
Jack we get de ring, for he know it.” De t’ree of dem come to Jack one
night and told Jack dat ’ey steal de ring. Jack said, “Oh, yes, I did
know a long time dat it you t’ief it!” Jack says, “If I tell de king
about de ring, king will behead de t’ree of you.” Jack says, “Make a
little ball and put de ring in it and put it down a big turkey’s
mout’.” De morning, nine o’clock, de king called Jack to tell him where
his wife’s ring goes; if Jack can not tell him, he will kill Jack. Jack
says, “If you want to know how you’ wife ring go, kill dat big turkey
an’ look in his craw.” Dey kill de turkey, an’ saw de ring; and from
dat day, de king believe what Jack do and give Jack his daughter to
marry. And I pass roun’ de house last week and I saw dem an’ dey give
me a good piece of beef-bone. Dear how Jack got his richness by working
his head!
paragraphs: Der was a day Jack says he was a fortune-teller. De king call him dat his wife los’ her marriage ring and he want him to tell him where it go. Jack didn’t know not’ing all de same, but jus’ working his head. De king got t’ree servant in his house. De t’ree of dem steal de ring. De king give Jack four days to tell him. One mo’ning, one carry Jack breakfas’. Jack says, “Praise de Lord, I got one!” Same day, one carry his dinner; same day, one carry his supper. Jack says, “Praise de Lord, I got de t’ree!” (Jack meant he get t’ree meals, but de servant think Jack mean them.) One of the servant go in the house, say, “Let us tell Jack we get de ring, for he know it.” De t’ree of dem come to Jack one night and told Jack dat ’ey steal de ring. Jack said, “Oh, yes, I did know a long time dat it you t’ief it!” Jack says, “If I tell de king about de ring, king will behead de t’ree of you.” Jack says, “Make a little ball and put de ring in it and put it down a big turkey’s mout’.” De morning, nine o’clock, de king called Jack to tell him where his wife’s ring goes; if Jack can not tell him, he will kill Jack. Jack says, “If you want to know how you’ wife ring go, kill dat big turkey an’ look in his craw.” Dey kill de turkey, an’ saw de ring; and from dat day, de king believe what Jack do and give Jack his daughter to marry. And I pass roun’ de house last week and I saw dem an’ dey give me a good piece of beef-bone. Dear how Jack got his richness by working his head!
語り手 T・ブラウン(セントアン、クレアモント)

ある日、ジャックが自分は占い師だと言った。王がジャックを呼んで、妻の婚礼の指環がなくなったので、どこへ行ったか当ててくれと言った。ジャックは何も知らなかったが、とにかく頭を絞っていた。王の家には召使いが三人いた。その三人が指環を盗んだのである。王はジャックに四日の猶予を与えた。ある朝、一人がジャックの朝飯を運んできた。ジャックは言う。「主に感謝、一つ手に入った!」 同じ日、一人が昼飯を運んできた。同じ日、一人が夕飯を運んできた。ジャックは言う。「主に感謝、三つとも手に入った!」(ジャックは三度の飯が手に入ったという意味だったが、召使いたちはジャックが自分たちのことを言ったと思った。)召使いの一人が家に入って言った。「ジャックに、おれたちが指環を取ったと言おう。あいつは知っているんだ」。三人はある晩ジャックのところへ来て、自分たちが指環を盗んだと打ち明けた。ジャックは言った。「ああ、そうとも。おまえたちが盗んだことは、とうの昔に知っていた!」 ジャックは言う。「おれが王さまに指環のことを話せば、王さまはおまえたち三人の首を刎ねるだろう」。ジャックは言った。「小さな団子をこしらえて、そのなかに指環を入れ、大きな七面鳥の口に入れておけ」。朝の九時、王はジャックを呼んで、妻の指環はどこへ行ったか言ってみろ、言えなければ殺すと言った。ジャックは言った。「奥方の指環がどこへ行ったか知りたければ、あの大きな七面鳥を絞めて、嗉嚢のなかをごらんなさい」。七面鳥を絞めると指環が出てきた。その日から王はジャックの言うことを信じるようになり、娘をジャックに娶らせた。先週わたしがその家のそばを通りかかったら二人がいて、いい牛骨を一本くれた。ああ、ジャックは頭を絞って身代を築いたのだ!
